stories.headline: The new economics of enterprise AI
stories.summary: Imagine your company just discovered electricity. At first only a few machines run on it, and nobody worries about efficiency — consumption is low and the value is obvious.
stories.why_it_matters: But once electricity becomes infrastructure, every process depends on it, and the question changes from “can we use it?” to “how efficiently are we using it?” Enterprise AI is going through the same shift. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: What began as isolated chatbot and copilot experiments is becoming a foundational layer of the business, with models, agents, and data increasingly interconnected in production workloads.

Technical Implementation: That’s the metric worth tracking: effective cost per useful outcome — the total platform, model, operations, and capacity cost required to complete work the business can actually use, whether a resolved request or a completed workflow.
Deployment & Impact: Directing more work to paid-for capacity lowers effective unit cost; idle GPUs, fragmented workloads, and oversized models all raise the cost of every useful result.

stories.headline: Better HTTP/1 connection reuse
stories.summary: The Go Blog Better HTTP/1 connection reuse Nicholas Husin and Damien Neil 14 October 2026 Take a look at the following function: func getStatus(url string) (int, error) { resp, err := http.Get(url) if err != nil { return 0, err } defer resp.Body.Close() return resp.StatusCode, nil } It sends a GET request to url and returns the HTTP status code. Using HTTP/1 ( GODEBUG=http2client=0 ), calling this function 100 times against index.golang.org takes ~710 milliseconds on Go 1.26 on my machine.
stories.why_it_matters: On Go 1.27, the same program takes ~150 milliseconds. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
key_points: Problem & Context: The Go Blog Better HTTP/1 connection reuse Nicholas Husin and Damien Neil 14 October 2026 Take a look at the following function: func getStatus(url string) (int, error) { resp, err := http.Get(url) if err != nil { return 0, err } defer resp.Body.Close() return resp.StatusCode, nil } It sends a GET request to url and returns the HTTP status code.

Technical Implementation: That is almost 5 times faster! How is such a drastic performance difference possible? The cost of establishing HTTP connections To understand the difference, consider what happens on the network when we make an HTTP request.
Deployment & Impact: Go’s net/http package supports HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, and HTTP/2.

stories.headline: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do

stories.headline: Introducing Amazon ECS Gateway: A fully-managed ingress solution for ECS services

stories.headline: Doing Less with More: A First-Principles Exploration of the Suitability of Agentic Computing over Alternative Architectural Choices
stories.summary: arXiv:2610.23921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There is growing interest in automating business activities with Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) due to latter's seeming ease of use. Never has it been easier, or costlier, to do less with more.
stories.why_it_matters: However, little is known about when agents are preferable to established alternatives such as local computation, Representational State Transfer (REST), the Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP), and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), particularly when development speed, performance, and operational cost are considered. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: However, little is known about when agents are preferable to established alternatives such as local computation, Representational State Transfer (REST), the Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP), and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), particularly when development speed, performance, and operational cost are considered.

Technical Implementation: We investigate this question using a controlled mathematical task that compares seven methods on a benchmark of 1,000 arithmetic expressions where semantics of operator precedence has to be preserved.

Deployment & Impact: We ran this setup across a native Function Calling baseline (Python library), REST, SOAP and MCP microservice architectures, direct responses from large language models (LLMs) using a Groq cloud API and five locally deployed Ollama models, and agentic systems in which five local LLMs invoke MCP tools.
